name: History of Concrete
description:
History of Concrete

PG | Documentary | 2026 | 102 min

After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, filmmaker John Wilson attempts to utilize the same commercial formula to create and sell a documentary about the history of concrete. The project evolves into a humorous and philosophical exploration of urbanism, the built environment, and the mundane textures of American life.

name: Retromania: Manhunter
description:
November Retromania (NEONvember): “Manhunter- The Final Cut 4K Restoration”

USA | Crime Thriller | 1986 | 119 min

A retired criminal profiler (William Petersen) reluctantly returns to the FBI to help track down a serial killer of families and is forced to consult an expert—the imprisoned Dr. Hannibal Lecktor (Brian Cox in a subtly chilling performance). The third feature written and directed by Michael Mann is a gripping adaptation of the first of Thomas Harris’s four novels featuring the iconic murderer Lecktor, and benefits from the filmmaker’s typically striking visuals as well as a top-notch supporting cast, including Tom Noonan as the hunted killer and three-time Oscar nominee Joan Allen as his blind love interest. This new 4K Final Cut, overseen by Mann, enhances the film’s depth, visual clarity and sound, offering audiences the ultimate immersive version.

name: Conan The Barbarian (CAMP! Series)
short_description:
Deanna Milligan & Ramsey Fendall

Caitlin Taylor

2025 / Canada / Horror, Fantasy/ 109min

Mia (Caitlin Acken Taylor) is a ’90s art student stuck in a creative muck, on the brink of being kicked out of art school and watching her life-long dreams shatter. Desperate to return to who she once was, she seeks out a magical Lucid Dreaming Elixir that promises inspiration but instead hurls her into a psychedelic whirlwind where the boundaries of reality, art, and identity dissolve.

In this dream-soaked universe, Mia – a fierce rebel-rouser with more attitude than direction -confronts surreal demons, fractured memories, and the long-buried traumas she’s spent years running from. The farther she runs, the deeper she falls into a chaotic subconscious labyrinth where monsters wear familiar faces and creativity demands a sacrifice she never expected.

Shot on lush 35mm and gritty Super 8, Lucid pulses with a visually salient, handcrafted aesthetic – equal parts punk, poetry, and nightmare. As Mia battles through dreams and delusions, she slowly discovers that becoming an artist isn’t about escaping the hole she’s fallen into, but understanding how it has shaped her. – DR
